items.title: Howard Johnson interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, January 14, 2019
items.q: But Red Callender taught Mingus to play the bass.

ctx.x: But Red Callender taught Mingus to play the bass. And so he was kind of angry and grumpy and everything else. And Jaki Byard, they were just about to take the stand and Jaki Byard said, “There’s your tuba player over there.” And Mingus, “You mean that kid?” Now at this point in the gig or whatever was going on, Mingus always called his band the Jazz Workshop. That gave him a chance to use anything you know. He could stop a band and rehearse a section that they didn’t get so well. He could change the key or change…
Oh so he used that as a —

items.q: I'm mailing some things to Bob Stewart and Howard Johnson. That's for five tubas and alto saxophone, flugelhorn and trombone and keyboards. I think it's going to be performed on September 20th

ctx.x: As a matter of fact, when I leave here today, I'm mailing some things to Bob Stewart and Howard Johnson. That's for five tubas and alto saxophone, flugelhorn and trombone and keyboards. I think it's going to be performed on September 20th, I don't know where, but in New York.
That should be interesting to hear.
